Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:1.english: With a mat of myrtle - A mat made of myrtle branches.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:2.hebrew: בד' זוזי דאית בה - כרוכים היו בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:2.english: With the four zuzim that are in it - They were wrapped in it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:3.hebrew: שקלתא - כלומר, נקטא לה ולא השלכתה, ואישתיקה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:3.english: She took it - That is to say, she held on to it and did not throw it down, and was silent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:4.hebrew: הויא שתיקה דלאחר מתן מעות - שמתחילה, כשקיבלתה והמעות היו בתוכה, לא ידעה בהן; וכשידעה אחר כן ושתקה — שתיקה דלאחר מתן מעות היא, ולאו כלום היא. דהאי דשתקה משום דלא איכפת לה, מימר אמרה: מעיקרא לאו אדעתיה דהכי קבילתינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:11:4.english: This is silence after the money is given - For initially, when she received it and the money was inside it, she did not know about it; and when she found out afterward and was silent — it is silence after the money is given, and it is nothing. For the fact that she was silent was because she did not care [to protest]; she said [to herself]: "From the outset, it was not with this in mind that I received them."

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:12:1.english: From where do I state this - That silence after the giving of money is nothing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:12:2.hebrew: בשעת מתן מעות - אם קודם שקבלתן אמר לה: ״התקדשי לי בו״ — מקודשת, דכי קבילתיה, אדעתא דהכי קבילתיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:12:2.english: At the time the money was given - If, before she received them, he said to her, “Be betrothed to me with it,” she is betrothed, for when she received it, [it was] with this intention that she received it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:13:1.english: By inference, the first clause - For it does not distinguish between [whether] she wanted and [whether] she did not want.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:1:1.hebrew: לאו היינו דיהודית - רב חסדא קאמר לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:1:1.english: Is this not the same as [the case of] Yehudit - Rav Chisda said this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:1:2.hebrew: צער לידה - שהיתה יולדת תאומים, דאמר מר (ביבמות דף סה:) יהודה וחזקיה אחי פזי וטוי אחוותא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:1:2.english: Pain of childbirth - For she would give birth to twins, as the Master said (in Yevamot, page 65b): Yehuda and Chizkiya, the brothers of Pazi and Tavi, were siblings.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:1:3.hebrew: קבל ביך אבוך קידושי - מאיש אחר, ובעל זה אסור לך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:1:3.english: Your father accepted betrothal on your behalf - from another man, and this husband [of yours] is forbidden to you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:2:1.hebrew: באידית - שם מקום. ואותו היום היו בכאן, והלכו להם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:2:1.english: In Idit - [This is] the name of a place. And on that day they were here, and [then] they went away.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:3:1.hebrew: דרבי חנינא - בכתובות, גבי בנתיה דשמואל דאשתביין, ואייתינהו לבי מדרשא דרבי חנינא, ואוקמינהו לשבוייהו אבראי. הא אמרה: נשביתי וטהורה אני, וכן אידך, והתירם לכהונה. ואמרו ליה לר' חנינא: הא איכא סהדי במדינת הים שראו אותן שנשבו, ותנן: אם יש עדים שנשבית, והיא אומרת: טהורה אני — אינה נאמנת! ואמר להו: השתא מיהא ליתנהו, ואינן מעידין על שבייתן, ונתירם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:3:1.english: Of Rabbi Ḥanina - In Ketubot, regarding the daughters of Shmuel who were taken captive: [the redeemers] brought them to the study hall of Rabbi Ḥanina and stationed their captors outside. One of them said, "I was taken captive and I am pure," and the other likewise, and he permitted them to [marry] into the priesthood. They said to Rabbi Ḥanina: But there are witnesses overseas who saw that they were taken captive, and we learned in a mishnah: If there are witnesses that she was taken captive, and she says, "I am pure," she is not believed! He said to them: Now, at any rate, they are not here, and they are not testifying about their captivity, so we permit them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:3:2.hebrew: עידיה בצד אסתן - רוח צפונית, ואינן באים ומעידים, ותאסר?! בתמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:3:2.english: Her witnesses are in the side of Istan - The northern direction, and they do not come and testify — and shall she be forbidden?! It is a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:4:1.hebrew: לא סבירא להו הא דרב חסדא - דאמר להתירה לשוק משום דאיכא סהדי באידית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:4:1.english: They do not hold this [statement] of Rav Chisda - [who said] to permit her [to remarry] because there are witnesses on the riverbank:

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:5:1.english: From that family - [This refers to the woman] who married another man and bore him [children].

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:5:2.hebrew: ולאו משום דסבירא להו דשמואל - למיחש שמא ש"פ במדי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:5:2.english: And it was not because they held like Shmuel - to be concerned that perhaps [the item is] worth a peruta in Media:

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:5:3.hebrew: אלא משום דסבירא להו דאביי ורבא - דכיון דאיכא סהדי באידית, לא מקילינן בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:5:3.english: Rather, because they held like Abaye and Rava - For since there are witnesses elsewhere, we do not act leniently with regard to it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:6:1.hebrew: בשוטיתא דאסא - בשבט בד של הדס:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:6:1.english: With a branch of myrtle - With a rod, a twig of myrtle.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:6:2.hebrew: נגדיה כרב - משום פריצותא דקדיש בשוקא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:6:2.english: Flog him, like Rav - Because of the licentiousness of one who betroths in the marketplace.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:6:3.hebrew: ואצרכה גיטא - אם באת לינשא לאחר, כשמואל דאמר: חיישינן שמא שוה פרוטה במדי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:6:3.english: And require her [to receive] a bill of divorce - If she comes to marry another, [this is] in accordance with Shmuel, who said: We are concerned that perhaps [the myrtle branch] is worth a peruta in Media.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:7:1.english: For Rav would flog, etc. - Because of immodesty.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:8:1.hebrew: ועל דמבטל גיטא - השולח גט לאשתו, והגיע הגט בשליח, ואמר לו המגרש לשליח: גט שנתתי לך בטל הוא. דילמא לא ידעי ליה אינשי דבטליה קודם שיבא לידה, ושמא יתננו השליח לאחר שבטלו, ותנשא בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:8:1.english: And for nullifying a bill of divorce - One who sends a bill of divorce to his wife, and [the bill] reached the messenger, and [the husband] said to [the messenger]: "The bill of divorce that I gave you is void." [This is prohibited] lest people not know that he nullified it before it comes into her hand, and perhaps the messenger will give it to her after [the husband] has nullified it, and she will marry on the basis of it:

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:8:2.hebrew: ועל דמסר מודעא אגיטא - כגון בגט המעושה בישראל, דמוציא לעז על בניה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:8:2.english: And for issuing a declaration concerning a bill of divorce - For example, with a bill of divorce [given] under duress by a Jew, [where one issues a declaration beforehand that he is being coerced,] for he thereby brings a bad name upon her children.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:8:3.hebrew: דמצער שליח דרבנן - שמזמינו לדין מפי הדיינין, וזה קם עליו ומכהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:8:3.english: For tormenting a messenger of the Sages - That [the messenger] summons him to judgment by the word of the judges, and this one rises against him and strikes him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:9:1.hebrew: ועל חתנא דדייר בבית חמוה - שמא יכשל בה, שסתם חמותה אוהבת את חתנה, דאמר מר (בפסחים דף קיג.): הוי זהיר באשתך מחתנה הראשון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:9:1.english: And concerning a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house - Lest he stumble with her [his mother-in-law], for a mother-in-law generally loves her son-in-law, as the Master said (in Pesachim, 113a): "Be careful with your wife regarding her first son-in-law."

Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:9:2.hebrew: מידם הות דיימא חמתיה מיניה - חשדוה ממנו. לשון דומה ובת דומה (סוטה דף כז.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 12b:9:2.english: There were suspicions about his mother-in-law and him - They suspected her of [misconduct] with him. [The term dayma is] an expression of dome (similarity), and [like the phrase] bat doma (Sotah 27a).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:10:1.hebrew: בכולהו לא מנגיד רב - על זה סומכין החתנים בזמן הזה שדרים בבית חמותם. ואפילו למאן דחייש לעיל — מה שדרין עכשיו בבית חמותם, היינו בשביל טובת הנאה שדרים בלא שכירות בבית; דיש הוכחה שאינם דרים בשביל חמותם, אלא בשביל שאר טובות שעושין להם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:10:1.english: "In all of them Rav would not flog" - On this the grooms rely nowadays, who live in the house of their mothers-in-law. And even according to the one who is concerned, above — that [grooms] now live in their mothers-in-law's house, this is for the sake of the benefit [they receive], that they live in the house without paying rent; for there is proof that they do not live [there] for the sake of their mothers-in-law, but rather for the sake of other benefits that [the in-laws] provide them:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:10:2.hebrew: משום פריצותא - מפרש ר"ת: דהיינו פריצותא, לפי שצריך או עדי ביאה או עדי יחוד, ודבר מכוער שמעמיד עדים על כך. וקשה, דביבמות פ' ר"ג (יבמות דף נב.) מייתי לה: מצות יבמה מקדש, והדר בעיל לא קדיש, לוקה מכת מרדות מדרבנן, כרב. והתם לאו משום עדים תליא טעמא, דהא יבמה מדאורייתא אינה נקנית אלא בביאה. אלא נראה לר"י דהיינו פריצות שעושין תחלת קניינן בביאה, דומיא דמקדש בלא שידוכי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:10:2.english: Due to licentiousness - Rabbeinu Tam explains: This is the licentiousness, because [the betrothal] requires either witnesses to the intercourse or witnesses to seclusion, and it is an indecent thing to stand witnesses over this. But this is difficult, for in Yevamot, in the chapter [beginning] Rabban Gamliel (Yevamot 52a), [the Gemara] cites it: [Regarding] the commandment of a yevamah — if he betroths [her] and afterward has intercourse [with her], [or] he has intercourse and does not betroth [her], he is flogged with rabbinic lashes for rebelliousness, in accordance with Rav. And there, the reason does not depend on witnesses, since a yevamah is, by Torah law, acquired only through intercourse. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that this is the licentiousness: that they make the beginning of their acquisition through intercourse, similar to one who betroths without a prior arrangement.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:12:1.hebrew: בשעת מתן מעות מקודשת - ה"ג, ולא גרסינן: "בין רצתה בין לא רצתה", כדאמר לקמן (קידושין דף יג.): "ליתני מקודשת סתם כי התם":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:12:1.english: "At the time the money was given, she is betrothed" - This is the correct reading, and we do not read: "Whether she wanted or did not want," as [the Gemara] says later (Kiddushin 13a): "Let it teach 'she is betrothed' without qualification, like there."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:2:1.hebrew: הא איכא סהדי באורית - ה"ג ר"ת, ולא גריס באידית, והסופרים טעו בין אידית לאורית. ואורית הוא מערב, כמו אוריה בפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כה.) גבי שכינה במערב: מאי אוריה? אויר יה. ולא כמו שפירש בקונטרס אוריה מזרח, אויר של פני השכינה. והשתא אתיא שפיר, דבני בבל היו אומרים: הא איכא סהדי באורי', כלומר בא"י שהוא מערב, כדאמרינן: במערבא אמרי, ורב חנינא מא"י אמר: עדיה בצד אסתן ותיאסר, כלומר בבל שהיא בצפון, דאסתן הוא צפון, כדאמרן (מגילה דף כח:): שמעתתא בעי צילותא כיומא דאיסתנא, דרוח צפונית מונעת את הגשמים, כדאמר (איוב ל״ז:כ״ב): מצפון זהב יאתה, תרגומא: מצפונא אסתנא יאתי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:2:1.english: "But there are witnesses in Urit" - So we read, [according to] Rabbeinu Tam, and he does not read "in Idit"; the scribes erred between Idit and Urit. And Urit is the west, like "Uriah" in the chapter Lo Yaḥpor (Bava Batra 25a), regarding the Divine Presence being in the west: What is "Uriah"? "The air of Yah." And [it is] not as Rashi explained in the commentary [that] Uriah is the east, the air of the face of the Divine Presence. And now it comes out well: the Babylonians were saying, "But there are witnesses in Uria," meaning in the Land of Israel, which is the west, as we say: "In the West they say," and Rav Ḥanina from the Land of Israel said: "Its witnesses are at the side of Astan, and she is forbidden," meaning Babylonia, which is in the north, for Astan is north, as we said (Megillah 28b): "Study requires shade, like the day of Istana," for the north wind holds back the rains, as it says (Job 37:22): "Gold comes from the north"; the Targum [renders]: "From the north, Astana, it comes."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:2:2.hebrew: והאיכא סהדי באורית - אין לפרש דניחוש לשמא איכא סהדי, דא"כ אין לדבר סוף, דלעולם איכא למיחש. והא נמי ליכא לפרש: והא איכא סהדי דידעי דבההוא שעתא הוה ביה ש"פ, דפשיטא דעל זה ראוי להחמיר. אלא נראה לר"י לפרש: והא איכא סהדי — כלומר, יצא הקול שיש עדים באורית או במדינת הים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:2:2.english: "But there are witnesses in Idit" - One cannot explain [this to mean] that we should be concerned lest there be witnesses, for if so, there would be no end to the matter, since there is always [room] for such a concern. Nor can one explain [the question] as: "But there are witnesses who know that at that time it was worth a peruta," for it is obvious that in such a case it is proper to rule stringently. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that [the Gemara's question] "But there are witnesses" should be explained as follows: that is, the word has gone out that there are witnesses in Idit or in a overseas country.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:4:1.hebrew: אם הקלנו בשבויה - אית ספרים שכתוב בהן: משום דמנוולא נפשה, נקל באשת איש? וי"מ: אם הקלנו בשבויה, היינו משום דאפילו איכא סהדי שנשבית, מ"מ לא היו יודעין אם נטמאה, א"כ אינה אסורה מה"ת (א"כ) — נקל באשת איש? דאי איכא סהדי דאותה אבנא דכוחלא אית בה ש"פ, הויא א"א גמורה, א"כ אין דין הוא שנקל עליה. וי"מ: אם הקלנו בשבויה משום דליכא אלא איסור לאו דזונה, נקל בא"א דאיכא איסור מיתה? ולא נהירא, שהרי השבויה נמי פעמים דאיכא איסור מיתה: אם הוא כהן, ויש לו בן ממנה שהוא חלל ויעבוד עבודה במזבח בשבת, ובזה יש חיוב מיתה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:4:1.english: "If we were lenient with regard to a captive woman" - There are books in which it is written: [If we were lenient] because she makes herself repulsive, shall we be lenient with regard to a married woman? Some explain: When [the Gemara says] "if we were lenient with regard to a captive woman," it is because even if there are witnesses that she was taken captive, nevertheless they would not know whether she was defiled; therefore she is not forbidden by Torah law. Shall we be lenient with regard to a married woman? For if there are witnesses that that stone within the kohl tube [i.e., a minimal act of relations] occurred, she is a fully [forbidden] married woman; therefore it is not right that we be lenient regarding her. And some explain: If we were lenient with regard to a captive woman because there is only the prohibition of a negative commandment of a zonah, shall we be lenient with regard to a married woman, where there is a prohibition [punishable by] death? But this is not clear, for with a captive woman too there are times when there is a prohibition [involving] death: if he is a priest, and he has a son from her who is a ḥalal, and [the son] performs service at the altar on Shabbat, and in this there is a death penalty.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:8:1.hebrew: ועל דמבטל גיטא - פ"ה: כגון השולח גט לאשתו והגיע בשליח, וא"ל: "גט שנתתי לך בטל הוא", ואיכא למיחש שמא יתננו לה השליח לאחר שבטלו ותנשא בו. ולא נהירא, דאין סברא לומר שיתן לה השליח כיון שהוא מוחה בו; דאטו ברשיעי עסקינן? לכן נ"ל כדאמר התם (גיטין דף לב.): "בראשונה היה עושה ב"ד ומבטל לפניהם, התקין ר"ג שלא יהו עושין כן". אך פליגי התם (דף לג.), דאיכא למ"ד אם בטלו מבוטל, ולדידיה ניחא, שהרי אשה זו אינה יודעת שבטלו ותינשא. ואפילו למ"ד התם אם בטלו אינו מבוטל, מ"מ הרי מוציא לעז על הגט:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 12b:8:1.english: "And for nullifying a bill of divorce" - Rashi explains: for example, one who sends a bill of divorce to his wife, and then, when the agent arrives, says to him, "The bill of divorce that I gave you is void." And there is reason to worry lest the agent give it to her after [the husband] has nullified it, and she would remarry on the basis of it. But this is not correct, for it is not reasonable to say that the agent would give it to her when [the husband] is protesting against it; are we dealing with wicked people? Therefore it seems to me [that the case is] as stated there (Gittin 32a): "Originally, one would set up a court and nullify [the bill of divorce] before them; Rabban Gamliel instituted that they should not do so." However, they disagree there (33a), for there is one who holds that if he nullified it, it is nullified, and according to him [the matter] is fine, since this woman does not know that he nullified it and she may remarry. And even according to the one who holds there that if he nullified it, it is not nullified, in any case he is casting a bad name upon the bill of divorce.
